title: Fazola's big band and the Plaza Club
summary: Personnel of the Fazola band, the Basin Street Six, and how he missed Fazola's record date.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Al Hurt, Julian Lane, Al's brother, Slick Hurt, and Johnny Ronica, myself. Who else? Steve Jarrett Tanner played tenor, and Fazola, four saxes. Al Hurt and who else now? Wimpy Miller, Wimp is a lawyer you know.
And I kind of remember the bass and the drums.
Well Charlie Duke played with him for a while. Charlie Duke, Charlie Duke, was it? Yeah I think Charlie was playing drums with us.
The Bonnie Franks played with him for a while.
Yeah, well it might have been those two, because then they later organized, made up that Basin Street Six, you see, and they joined them.
It seems to me that's just about the same band that recorded for Victor. The Basin Street Six? No, the Fazola band recorded for Victor.
Well I didn't make recordings with him, because I think he made recordings later. I was playing at the St. Charles Stadium, and he just got more or less the same group that he had before, you see.
Well they were playing at the, see I was down here in 45 and 46, I was in the Navy, and I heard Fazola at the Plaza Club. Yeah that's the place.
Were you working with him? Yeah I worked at the Plaza with him.
And then after that he made the record, back in Georgia.

Yeah I remember now, later. The record was made later, and I couldn't make it because I was tied up in a two-year theater from one o'clock in the afternoon to eleven at night, you know, four shows a day.

Yeah, I might have heard you when I was in the Navy and didn't know you then. I remember talking to Charlie Duke out there. I think it was his wife or his girlfriend who introduced me to him. At the time I was still interested in, very interested in the band.
